page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-64 is an arm64-based server instance powered by the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz with a single thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory performance. The instance achieved a top-tier rating in passmark memory score and database operations, alongside a top-tier bzip3 multi-threaded decompression speed of 717.79 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests show top-tier performance for cached small blocks at 7912.04 GB/sec and strong performance for uncached large blocks. In compute-heavy tasks, the server demonstrated top-tier results in software compilation, image processing, and physics simulations. However, single-core stress-ng performance and text processing benchmarks remain in the average tier.

The c4a-highmem-64 offers high resource density for memory-intensive workloads without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU hardware. The combination of dedicated Neoverse-V2 cores and high memory bandwidth makes this instance highly efficient for database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and memory-bound enterprise applications. It is also well-suited for lightweight LLM inference tasks, demonstrating strong text generation speeds on medium-sized models, though it lacks the hardware acceleration required for larger-scale AI workloads.
